idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy in all regions and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before trying to deploy it again.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. The test version of v2.3.1 had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions, health checks pass and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 says what failed, that we rolled back to v2.3.0 and how the service looks now. It also says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before anyone deploys it again. The first attempt to open the incident timed out. I checked that nothing had been created, then retried with the same idempotency key, which stops a duplicate from being created.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.

content.text:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. The test version of v2.3.1 had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions, health checks pass and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 says what failed, that we rolled back to v2.3.0 and how the service looks now. It also says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before anyone deploys it again. The first attempt to open the incident timed out. I checked that nothing had been created, then retried with the same idempotency key, which stops a duplicate from being created.
